entries.text: A startup death's card now always names the death's category and stage coordinate. The bare "exited during startup" line was all a non-crash death ever showed: the system publishes the process exit record asynchronously, and it routinely missed the few seconds the card waited for it, so the record was filtered away as stale and nothing was appended at all. The card now always closes with diagnostic lines gated to this attempt: the newest exit record's category line — its reason, status or signal, time and description — or an explicit line saying the record is not published yet; the last stage mark the core left behind, whatever the death turns out to be; the first line of a crash report fresh enough to belong to this attempt, or a note that there is none; and the daemon log's last error line, when it has one. The wait for the record is widened to about five seconds, still far inside the start budget.

The service log's death block now quotes the stage-marker trail for any surfaced exit record, not only Go crashes. The marks are how a death gets its stage coordinate — the last phase the core reached before it died — but they were appended inside the crash-gated part of the block, so a death by signal or by the low-memory killer left the service log as bare as the card. Any new exit record being surfaced now carries the marks with it, written once even when a crash block follows.

The sing-box core no longer panics on a cellular interface's link-local IPv6 address. Interface prefixes handed to the core were built straight from the platform's address string, and a link-local address carries its zone along — fe80::…%rmnet_data1/64 — which the core's prefix parser rejects outright: IPv6 zones cannot be present in a prefix, raised as a panic inside the interface refresh that every monitor update runs, so the first update whose enumeration included the cellular interface killed the start. Interface prefixes are now rebuilt from the address's raw bytes before they are handed over, which strips the zone while keeping the address and its prefix length intact — the shape the reference client has always used. IPv4 prefixes are unchanged.

The sing-box interface monitor now warms up before a start and cannot lose a delivery in silence. Registration used to sit inside the start path, a breath ahead of the start itself, and the core could come up before any platform update had ever reached it — its interface list stayed empty and every dial in the rule-set downloads that follow a start reported no available network interface. The monitor registers when the service is created now, so the system's updates collect in the serialized lane ahead of any start; attaching a listener primes it from the network the system reports at that moment, seeded and replayed in one lane step, never from a snapshot taken at registration time. And a delivery whose link properties are not readable yet is no longer dropped: the cleared reading is delivered instead, which still has the core refresh its interface list, and the reading that lands later corrects the default.

The crash report's first line now closes the death block in the service log. A native death already surfaced the report's head, its tail and the stage-marker trail, but the line that names the failure sits at the top of that block — above the window a failure card shows. The last line of the block is now a crash reason line carrying the report's first non-empty line verbatim, so the reason reads off the card directly; a report that is missing or unreadable leaves a one-line note saying so.

The sing-box default-interface monitor now delivers the way the reference client delivers. Interface callbacks used to report from whichever system thread delivered them, straight into the core, while a start was still setting up; updates now pass through one serialized lane owned by the service — the system callbacks only post, link properties are read on the lane, and the core hears about the tracked network in arrival order, replayed to a listener that attaches late. Registration itself sits at the service layer, happens once per service lifetime ahead of the start, and is tiered by platform level the way the reference client tiers it; a report always carries the unmetered, unconstrained reading.

The interface monitor seeds before it registers. The monitor's initial state used to be queued after the system callback was registered, so the system's first update could land ahead of the seed and then be overwritten by the older snapshot; the seed is queued first now, and the first system update always lands on top of it.

A native death's crash report now shows its head as well as its tail. The service log carried only the report's last lines — the end of a goroutine stack — while the line that names the failure sits at the top of the file; when a death leaves a report tail, the head's first forty lines now land in the log ahead of it under a crash head prefix, and a report that cannot be read leaves a one-line note saying so instead of silence.

The stage-marker trail joins the crash report in the service log. The instrumented core writes a line at each start stage it reaches; when a native death leaves a crash tail, the last thirty marker lines now land in the log behind it under a stage mark prefix, so the stage the start had reached when it died reads off the log directly. A death that left no markers leaves no marker lines.

The sing-box core is bound with the stage-marker patches applied. The bind that builds the core library from its pinned source now applies four small patches after the source sync — a marker writer, marks at the daemon's and the box's start boundaries and across the interface monitor's update path, and the marker file's path set during setup — and asserts every landing spot before the build proceeds, so an upstream change that moves a context line fails the build loudly instead of shipping an uninstrumented core. The patches live in the repository; the core source and the built library never do.

The core switch card takes the cabin panel shadow. The general settings page's core switch card already sat on the cabin card corner with the rim, but it lay flat where its dashboard sibling is lifted by the panel shadow; it takes the same shadow now, from the same surface definition, so the two presentations of the one switch read as one card. Nothing inside the card moved — title, status sentence, failure detail, the binary area, the two core rows and every callback are byte-identical.

The profile editor's core selector reads like the switch card. The editor used to pick a profile's core kind from a bare dropdown while the general page presents the same choice as two rows on the switch card; the editor now presents the two cores as card rows in that language — the core disc mark, the shared display name (sing-box keeps its hyphen), the running state and the selection check on the chosen row, which is inert, while the other row makes the same one call the dropdown made. The two platform captions keep their wording and their conditions and move inside the card.

The disclaimer body takes a cabin panel. The disclaimer text used to read flat on the page; it now sits in a raised cabin panel — card corner, rim and panel shadow — with its wording unchanged. The consent bar below it is untouched.

The about page's marks settle into the cabin language. The logo well gains the cabin rim, and the version pill — a solid primary fill — now reads as a marker chip: a raised surface carrying primary text, the way markers read everywhere else in the cabin, instead of a lone filled badge.

Dialog and menu shapes take the cabin rim at the theme base. Dialogs, popup menus and menus already shared the floating corner; their theme shapes now carry the cabin rim side as well, defined in the one place all three shapes live, so every overlay the bases present is rimmed and there is no second definition anywhere to drift from it.

The popup card takes the floating corner and a rim on its plain fill. The morphing popup card sat on a corner one step under the floating tier the other overlays settled on; it takes the floating corner now, its rows concentric inside it, and its plain fill — the non-glass reading — gains the cabin rim. The glass path is unchanged.

Sheet top corners settle on the floating corner. A sheet's crown sat one tier rounder than the dialogs and menus it appears beside; the snap sheet, the paged sheet and the theme's bottom-sheet shape now all take the floating corner, so every floating surface in the app crowns at the same radius.

The segmented control's chosen face takes the ink variant. The selected segment used to fill with the accent; it now fills with ink and its label takes the page step — the quieter reading the cabin reserves for a mode choice — at the two places the control serves: the theme page's mode strip and the palette's core segments. No other surface takes the variant.

Error faces settle to plan B: red stays on the glyph and the words. The error banner's container was the error fill; it now sits on a neutral raised surface with the cabin rim, its icon and text carrying the error color. The error illustration's body returns to the neutral surface steps, red surviving only in the central glyph. The fatal start-up error screen keeps its full red face by design — plan B grades the everyday error faces, not the fatal one.

A concurrent delete that reaches the same end state is no longer an error. Deleting a file checked that it existed and then deleted it, so two callers clearing the same cache file at once raced: the loser was handed a file-not-found exception for an absence that was exactly what it had asked for, and the spurious failure once reddened a release build's test run after the test itself had already completed. Deletion now treats 'already gone' as the contract fulfilled; every other failure still propagates.

The record rows take the cabin row-card corner. The shared record row card — the one row the requests, connections, DNS queries and log screens are all built from — sat on the section-card corner and carried no rim, while every other cabin plate pairs its corner tier with the cabin rim. It drops to the row-card corner and gains the rim side, so the record lines read as cabin row cards like the rest of the interface; the wide-screen record tables already sat on the card step and keep it, and status chips, rates and every row action are untouched.

Log payloads sit in an inset well. A log entry's payload no longer reads flat on its row card: it recesses into a rimmed inset well — the same well form the profile payload took in the configuration line — with the entry's header staying on the card outside it. The level mark stays a small chip at the head of the row, its color the only color the row carries, and the payload text keeps its monospace step.

The theme preview shows both cabins at once. The live preview no longer renders a single mini screen in the app's current brightness: the light scheme on the paper phone and the dark scheme on the dark phone stand side by side, sharing the one selection and animation state, so a scheme can be judged in both cabins before it is picked. The preview plate itself takes the cabin rim.

The theme page's plates take the rim, and the swatch marker stops changing color. The color swatch selection ring used to take each swatch's own fill, so the selected marker changed color with the swatch it sat on; it now stays on the scheme primary for every swatch, the way a marker should — the one accent the page allows itself. The page's bespoke plates — the swatch box, the font card, the text-scale plate and the custom-color preview — gain the cabin rim, their ink and layouts unchanged.

The hotkey page's intro plate takes the cabin rim — the one bespoke plate on that page still missing it, now in line with the rest. The keycaps stay on the block step in monospace, and the conflict reading keeps the form the settings screens settled on.

The DNS queries empty state takes the brand variant. Where the empty DNS list used to show the functional illustration, it now shows the gray disc mark the cabin language reserves for brand positions — the same motif the dashboard's core carries — with its label unchanged.

Signaled sing-box deaths now arm the staged ladder and the cache isolation. Three full starts in a row died about a tenth of a second after the start call — two of them classified by the system as signaled deaths rather than native crashes — and the ladder never ran for the signaled pair, because the arming set and the cache-isolation gate both recognized only native crashes and low-memory kills. A signaled death at the same code point, with the same memory snapshot, is the same start failure under the system's other label — the crash pipeline simply filed no tombstone for it — so signaled deaths arm both gates now, and the isolation predicate lives in one place the two gates share; the isolation log line names its cause and stays byte-identical for native crashes.

Signaled deaths are named by their signal, and the death card waits out the tombstone on one clock. The exit record has carried the killing signal's number all along; the card now reads it and names it, so a signaled death reads SIGNALED with its SIGSEGV, SIGKILL, SIGBUS, SIGABRT or SIGILL beside it — and whether a signaled death and a native crash at the same point are one death wearing two labels can finally be judged from the card. The crash headline's hunt no longer swallows its misses, either: when a native crash's trace cannot be read, the service log says which of the three ways it missed — the trace stream was unavailable, the trace was unreadable, or it held no signal line — on both channels that report a death. And the card's assembly now waits on a single shared budget for the attempt's record and, behind a native crash, for the headline, instead of the two racing separately; a settled record whose death is not a native crash stops waiting at once.

A render-side preflight rejection now says why. When a profile cannot be converted for sing-box because nothing in it is usable, the switch used to cancel with the bare 'cannot be converted' line and the reason nowhere on the card. The rejection now carries the renderer's own count: how many nodes speak protocols sing-box does not support — named by their own protocol strings — how many are wireguard nodes it cannot use, how many groups have no usable member, and how many unsupported group types, skipped REJECT members and untranslated rules account for the rest. A profile with nothing convertible at all gets its own plain sentence, and content that is not a recognizable Clash configuration at all gets another. The verdict itself has not moved — the same profiles are refused — but the refusal explains itself.

The configuration list's current profile takes the cabin reading the dashboard set: the card grows the disc watermark at its top end — the same motif, at the same size and faintness, as the dashboard's current-profile card — and the in-use mark moves out of the generic selection badge into a dedicated metadata chip, accent text on the block step, while expiry and the other identity chips stay on their neutral ground. Selection, pressing and the card's data flow are untouched, and the add-profile page rides along unchanged on the shared card language.

The universal import page sits its payloads in wells built from the cabin surface steps: the URL field and the pasted-text field recess into inset wells behind the rim border, and the parsed result rises into a block-step well inside the card, so an imported payload reads as set into the page rather than typed over it. The guide head — disc motif and a status-style title — and the single primary confirm button were already the signed-off reading and stay; controllers, parsing and every callback are untouched.

A geometry correction rides with the import wells: their decoration now draws the project's superellipse border — the rounded-superellipse shape the cards and the Dock already use — instead of a plain circular-arc box, so the wells' corners sit on the one corner geometry the interface allows itself. Radius, rim color, step color and padding are unchanged; only the corner curve moved.

The node exit-IP type probing added with the proxies cabin batch is removed end to end, on the strength of the device verdict: on the profiles it served — OpenVPN home-broadband nodes — the per-node probes timed out in bulk and the rows sat on the probing placeholder with the type never landing. The proxies rows lose the type mark, the probing placeholder and the first-visit note; the page-entry sweep, the delay-test piggyback probes and the per-profile node-to-IP disk map are gone, and the settings switch and the long-press re-probe go with them. The page keeps its cabin form — row-card radius, the selected card's cyan rim and dot, the group metadata chips — and the dashboard's current-exit panel, which predates the module and reads only the connection in use, is not touched.

The sing-box renderer likewise gives back the probe channel it had injected for the removed module: renders no longer add the probe selector over all leaf outbounds, the loopback mixed inbound on port 17909, or the binding rule that rode at the head of the route, so the rendered config is again exactly the pre-probe one, its route rules back to seven — and a guard test now sweeps every rendered tag and the encoded text for any probe remnant. The probe client that switched the injected group is deleted with it.

The sing-box death card no longer loses its own verdict to a race: a crash's exit record is published by the system only after the process has died, and the card used to read it exactly once — too early, it found only the previous attempt's record, failed the attempt association and fell back to the bare generic line, so the signal headline and the attempt line never reached the card. The plugin now waits a bounded grace — thirteen probes over about three seconds — for a record that belongs to this attempt, and only silence still settles for the generic line; a failure card can arrive those three seconds later, carrying strictly more. The same commit stops the service log from printing the crash-report tail header over an empty tail: header and lines now appear only when there is a tail to show.

The proxies page now marks every node with the type of the exit IP it really uses: a sweeper resolves each node's exit address — on mihomo through the existing routed probe, on sing-box through a probe channel the renderer injects additively (a dedicated selector over all leaf outbounds, a loopback mixed inbound and one binding rule; strip the three additions and the render is byte-identical to before) — classifies the address through the shared six-source quality lookup, and persists the node-to-IP map per profile for twenty-four hours, invalidated the moment the profile or the running core changes. A row whose type is known carries a small neutral chip — residential, data center or mobile — a group row reads the type of the leaf it actually exits through, and while a type is unknown the row shows nothing at all: a type is never guessed from a node's name. A settings switch turns the whole module off, and a long press on a mark re-probes that one node.

The proxies page takes the cabin reading: node cards settle on the 20-unit row-card radius, the selected card gains the signal-cyan rim overlay and the 7px cyan dot beside its name, and group types move out of plain text into neutral metadata chips, while the exit-IP quality sheet behind a mark stays the existing one.

Two follow-up corrections ride with the batch: the first-visit note about IP types now floats over the proxies list instead of flowing above it, so its asynchronous arrival no longer shifts the list geometry under the reader; and the sweeper no longer unwatches the routed probe when a widget tears down — its entries ride the probe until a core or profile reset — which keeps a teardown from synchronously detaching the probe's transport as its last consumer leaves.

The staged sing-box start ladder now probes two levels below the bare instance: L-1 starts the bare form with the cache file redirected to a fresh probe file (cache-probe-<seq>.db) in the same working directory — the daemon passes a platform log writer unconditionally, so the cache file is opened at every level and only its path can be moved — and L-2 starts a literal near-empty config, a log level and one direct outbound, derived from nothing the renderer or the trimming code produced. Stale probe files are swept before the ladder runs, and the verdicts name the new levels: a death at L-1 clears the cache file's contents (a virgin file crashed on first touch, so suspicion moves to the hosting layer), a death at L-2 after L-1 passed convicts the cache (the torn default cache file is the one material thing the level restores), and a death at L0 after both passed narrows the next round to the bare form's own construction.

The sing-box death card now leads with the tombstone's own evidence instead of the log tail: the signal line comes first — signal, code and fault address — followed by a plain-language note where the signal carries one (SIGBUS points most often at a damaged memory-mapped file such as the cache file, SIGSEGV at a native invalid memory access, SIGABRT at a deliberate abort such as a Go runtime fatal) and the first backtrace frame, joined to the verdict ahead of the attempt line. The register rows that used to crowd the card stay in the full service log, where trace excerpts are now prefixed line by line and the card's tail filters those lines out.

A sing-box config check that goes unanswered is no longer reported as an unconvertible profile: the plugin retries a silent check once under a fresh request id — re-sending the intent itself restarts a dead service process, and a late answer to the first attempt can never be taken for the retry's — and only two silences in a row settle the matter, as a new failure that says the service did not respond and that this does not mean the config is invalid. A real validation answer, empty or an error string, is still taken the first time and still names the profile; the Dart-side check budget rises from 35 to 75 seconds to cover both attempts.

A sing-box process death is now charged to the start attempt that owned it: every attempt carries a sequence number, written with its ledger entry and mirrored where the main process can read it, and an exit record is only quoted when it falls inside the attempt's own five-second association window — a verdict that belongs to this tap reads 'attempt #<n> died: LOW_MEMORY(3) at …', the matching line in the service log gains the same attempt suffix, and an earlier death, an idle-time reclaim or a record that has not landed yet is never presented as this tap's failure again

The staged start ladder is now armed for low-memory kills as well as native crashes: an attempt death the system records as LOW_MEMORY inside its window sends the next start down the same trimmed levels, and the verdict names the cause as well as the level — 'staged start: low-memory killed at L<k> (<name>)' — with the full-config level stating plainly that the whole start's peak is in question; deaths that are neither a native crash nor a low-memory kill still leave the ladder unarmed

Every real start now leaves a memory snapshot in the service log immediately before it runs — 'start: memory snapshot: pss <x> MB, avail <y> MB, lowMemory=<bool>' — and each staged level's begin line carries that level's own PSS, so the level whose start first inflates memory is visible in the numbers next to the moment it happened, and the system's free-memory and low-memory readings at the time stand as the pressure evidence beside any kill

A sing-box working cache left behind by a native crash no longer poisons every later start: before any start that follows a recorded native-crash exit, the cache file in the core's working directory is renamed aside exactly once, keeping one rolled-aside copy, so a cache torn by a process killed mid-write cannot crash the next start the same way; starts after any other kind of exit, and every healthy start, never touch the cache

A native crash during a full sing-box start is now bisected instead of repeated blindly: the crashed attempt is remembered in a ledger written synchronously, so it survives the dying process, and the next start walks trimmed-down configurations built from the same rendered config — bare direct, then outbounds and DNS, then rule sets, then inbounds, then the untouched full config — each level pre-checked before it runs, narrowing the crash to the stage whose component set first brings it back

When a staged level crashes, the tap after it starts nothing: it fails in writing with the crashed level named — 'staged start: crashed at L<k> (<name>)' — in the switch card and the service log, and the attempt after that returns to the normal full start; a level that merely returns an error stays an ordinary failure, never a crash verdict, and a trimmed config that fails its check quietly falls back to the full start

The process-death verdict now carries the tombstone's signal line when the system provides one: the first signal line — signal number and name, code and fault address — is extracted and appended to the exit summary in the service log and the switch card's failure detail, so a crash reports whether it was a bus error at a mapped page, a segmentation fault or an abort; when no trace is available, the summary stands on its own as before

A failed sing-box start now names the recorded cause of the process death instead of only reporting that the process exited: on every service start the newest system process exit record for the sing-box process is read, and its reason — a native crash, low memory, a signal and the rest of the platform set — is written to the service log and folded into the switch card's failure detail, so the next failure reads its exit reason on the card itself

The Go crash report the core's error output is redirected to is now read back instead of sitting unread in the working directory: its last forty lines join the service log once per change alongside the exit record, so a fatal crash inside the core leaves its stack where the failure detail and the next diagnosis can reach it

Errors escaping the sing-box start and profile check paths are no longer silent: both catches are widened from exceptions to all throwables, so an escaping error now fails the attempt in writing — a failed state and a log line — instead of the start thread vanishing without a trace and leaving only a timeout or a dead-process verdict behind, and the service's reload entry gains begin, returned and failed markers with the same treatment

Both themes gain pinned surface ladders ahead of the cabin restyle: the dark steps settle at the deep values — page #090B0C, card #161818, block #202223 — and the light theme trades its one shared surface role for a warm paper ladder, a paper page under a pure white card with a warm white block inside, so pages, cards and inset blocks separate into three readable levels in both themes

The cabin token layer is declared: card corners settle at 22, row cards at 20 and a new floating tier at 26 covers the dock, dialogs and menus; panel borders read as a rim highlight — white at 7% in dark, ink at 6% in light — and soft panel and dock shadow pairs are fixed for both themes, with common cards taking the rim and the 22 corner now and the shadows following screen by screen

Navigation takes its cabin forms: the floating dock stands 70 high with 26 corners on the chrome step, a rim edge and the dock shadow, its lens tinted in ink instead of the signal colour with a 5 px signal dot marking the selected entry; the edge navigation bar keeps its body on the chrome step with an ink selection reading, and the desktop sidebar selects in ink with its signal marker kept and its inner dividers in the rim tone

The shared type scale is settled: page titles at 27, list titles at 15 medium, subtitles at 12, captions at 11 and card headers at 16 semibold, declared at one point and inherited by every screen instead of each surface keeping its own sizes

A sing-box start whose service process dies mid-start is now called as what it is within one polling cycle instead of pending for the whole 40 seconds: the start gate checks the starting snapshot's process id, and a dead process fails the attempt at once with a detail that says the process exited during start, while an unknown process id still reads as pending

When a sing-box start times out, the attempt is now stopped and invalidated instead of being left to finish unwatched: the plugin sends an explicit stop, the service voids the attempt and frees the start gate, and a start that completes late tears itself down without writing a stale running or failed state over the next attempt, so one hung start can no longer poison every retry until the process is killed

The sing-box service's own log is now persisted and reaches the failure message: the box log is forwarded and written with stage markers to a rolling 256 KB service log on disk, and a failed start appends its last six lines to the detail under the plain-language sentence, so a start failure finally shows where the core stopped instead of only reporting a timeout

The rest of the profiles line joins the settled card and form standards: an empty profile list shows the brand disc mark, the expiry and group count chips read neutral with red kept only for an expiry that has already passed, and the universal import page gathers its import methods and its name and template fields into section cards under a disc header, with errors in the standard banner and the parse result in a titled section

The logs page payload now reads in the monospace type scale end to end — message, tag, destination, error, rule, arrow and source — and the routed proxy name drops the signal colour for a neutral emphasis, matching how record rows mark chain names; the requests, connections, DNS and resources screens were audited onto the same record row standards

The theme page's font and text-scale cards take the card corner tier and its sidebar blur row sits in a section card, and the hotkey page reads an unbound row in the variant tone instead of the outline tone, warns on a recording conflict in the warning tone, keeps its intro glyph neutral, and sets key caps in tabular figures

Value-level marks in the rule and filter forms drop the tertiary colour, which sits outside the settled semantic palette: neutral rule outcomes such as PASS, GLOBAL and MATCH, the filter regex caption, the rule preset subtitle and the custom profile status now read in the neutral variant or surface tone, while DIRECT keeps success, the REJECT family keeps warning and an invalid value keeps error

Member type chips in the custom group editor sit on the neutral raised step with variant text, matching the settled tonal chip, instead of the secondary and tertiary container colours; only an exclude member keeps the error container reading

Core switching on Android now trusts only the current attempt's native answers: every sing-box start stamps the status snapshot with its own epoch, so a previous failure can no longer answer every later retry within milliseconds and a dead process's leftover RUNNING can no longer pass as success; the service channel waits for each start and stop request's real outcome in the native state machine before it replies; a start counts only once the core's own API probes back; starts are single-flight, the service no longer resurrects its previous configuration after being killed, and the native and Dart start budgets are aligned at 40 and 45 seconds so the native verdict is always the one acted on; and on Windows a switch first reclaims this app's own orphaned sing-box processes and waits for the mixed port to free before the new core spawns

The sing-box configuration the app renders no longer contains the legacy block outbound that sing-box removed in 1.13 and the bundled 1.14.4 rejects outright: REJECT group members are dropped with a note, a MATCH out to REJECT becomes a trailing reject rule instead, and the rendered configuration is strictly validated with Libbox.checkConfig before any core is stopped, so a profile the bundled sing-box cannot accept is refused up front, in the checker's own words, instead of burning a switch on it

The core switch card drops the stock segmented button, which sat inside it like a foreign widget, for two rows in the card's own language — a block-tier fill, the disc motif as the row mark in the signal colour only on the selected core, the core's name and running state, and the shared selection check — and a failed switch now shows the native detail (a libbox rejection, a service failure) in small type under its plain-language sentence instead of discarding it

The add-profile page gathers its five entries — QR code, file, link, custom and universal import — from bare rows on the page fill into one grouped card that shares the dashboard and settings surface step, corner tier and hairlines, with the universal import row taking the page's single accent spot, a sparkle glyph in the primary colour, instead of a second copy of the file glyph

The sing-box card in Settings is now a core switch with a mihomo / sing-box segmented control: one tap stops the running core, starts the target and re-applies the current profile for it, naming each stage as it goes, and the current profile is rendered for the target core up front, so one that cannot be converted is refused before anything stops

Starting sing-box on Android while mihomo was running no longer hangs and then fails with a raw error claiming mihomo could not stop: the switch stops mihomo through the real run-state chain, the stopped state is written back where the rest of the app reads it, and a stop that does not take effect no longer leaves every other core action reporting the core as not connected

When a core switch fails part-way through, the core that ran before is restored, and the card explains in one plain sentence which step failed and what to do next, instead of surfacing the raw exception

The proxies page joins the settled interface standards: node cards sit on the neutral surface at the card corner step, the signal colour stays only on functional marks such as the current node and the selected group, and delays read as small labels in semantic colours
Beginner mode is removed: every install now gets the full dashboard, and the import card on the home screen is simply the empty state shown to everyone while no profile exists yet
The sing-box section in Settings now keeps everything inside its card — status, the binary location, download progress with the route in use, and any error — instead of spilling rows below it

Downloading the sing-box binary now tries the Windows system proxy first, then a running core, then a direct connection, with a timeout on each hop and partial downloads cleaned up, instead of going direct and hanging until it times out
When the core is not connected, profile actions no longer claim it returned an empty profile; they say the core is not connected and ask for it to be started first

The shared interface kit is settled ahead of the screen-by-screen restyle: title weights step down a grade, body text gets a little more line height, large numbers use tabular figures, and cards, blocks and chips follow declared corner steps
Empty states gain a brand variant that carries the disc mark, and dialogs and bottom sheets now rest on one declared base

The sing-box core now takes care of itself on Windows: if the binary is missing, Settings offers a one-tap download of the pinned release, verified by checksum, into the app data folder, and starting a sing-box profile fetches it automatically — upgrades no longer lose it
Profile downloads route through the running sing-box core too, which ends the add-profile timeouts that hit whenever sing-box was in charge and no other core was running
The dashboard editor lists the addable cards at the top instead of below every card already shown, and says so when every card has been added
Desktop dashboard cards refill their row when a card is removed, instead of leaving an empty gap behind

The YouTube service check probes a lightweight endpoint first and only then judges the region, so a slow premium page no longer shows up as a timeout; a failed check also retries once instead of staying frozen
When the core is stopped, the status and service cards label their results as direct-route readings instead of presenting them as the selected node's
The Android notification and quick-settings tile icons now use the KFusion disc rather than the leftover upstream glyph
The phone home has a new hierarchy: the current node, speed and profile cards lead, and the status card carries the logo's disc-and-bite motif
Beginner mode narrows the home to the core cards, and with no profile yet a universal-import guide card leads the first setup instead of an empty dashboard
The desktop dashboard now shares the phone's saved card list: cards can be removed, added back and reordered on desktop too, instead of a fixed layout

New PC icon set in the outlined-disc scheme: the Windows app, installer and shortcut icons drop the white tile for the T disc on transparency with a light outline, and the tray icons are discs too — grey when stopped, black when running, a gold ring while TUN is on and orange in safe mode
The bite cut out of the disc is filled white instead of showing through, so it stays readable on dark wallpapers across the app and tray icons
A new look that matches the T disc logo: a signal-cyan accent over near-neutral black, white and grey surfaces, with light and dark following the system by default

Universal import has real action buttons now: download and parse, choose file and parse text sit under their fields instead of hiding in the section header rows, and a disabled confirm button shows where the import will be confirmed before anything is parsed
The Windows install no longer carries FlClash names: the core and helper binaries are KFusionCore.exe and KFusionHelperService.exe, helper service name included
The desktop entry written for protocol registration is named KFusion, the last visible piece of the rename

Fix sing-box profile activation failing against the bundled sing-box 1.14 runtime: the renderer now emits the 1.14 configuration format (typed DNS servers with a fakeip server and a DNS hijack rule action, rule-set based GEOIP and GEOSITE rules, the TUN address list, WireGuard endpoints and the experimental cache file) instead of the removed pre-1.12 formats
Map the Clash built-in policies when rendering sing-box groups and rules: DIRECT and REJECT group members resolve to the direct and block outbounds, and REJECT rule targets become reject rule actions

Fix the crash on launch: the app manifest now names the application and component classes the app actually ships, instead of classes resolved from the renamed application id namespace, which did not exist
Fix the platform channel prefix mismatch left over from the rename, so the Dart side reaches the app, battery, service and tile channels the native side registers
Android sing-box runtime: libbox built from the pinned sing-box source in Gradle and hosted by SingBoxVpnService, with two-way exclusion against the mihomo core
The Android sing-box service runs on the libbox command server, the entry point of sing-box 1.14
The libbox and mihomo gomobile runtimes coexist in one package: a single shared Seq copy at runtime, with the libbox bindings compiled against a compile-only Seq jar
KFusion baseline on the FlClash base: Android and Windows only, rebranded as an independent app

Second core: sing-box rendering and a Windows sidecar runtime, mutually exclusive with the mihomo core
